articles.title: Women face bans on research underground — here’s how to modernize the system
articles.summary: Nature, Published online: 27 August 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-02679-yIn many countries, female engineers are barred from entering deep mines to carry out studies. Differentiating risks can increase access while protecting safety.
articles.content:
When I began my research career nearly a decade ago, there were no female academics in the mining-engineering department at Central South University in Changsha, China. Only this year did the department appoint me as its first female professor. I welcome that change, but it shows that the expectations around who can pursue mining careers have only recently begun to shift.

I have visited many mines for research and fieldwork, in China and abroad, only to be told that I could not go underground. Sometimes, this happened after I had already planned the work and travelled there. The situation felt absurd: a researcher who helped to design a monitoring or warning system for a deep mine could not see the environment that it would operate in.

How to widen access to the critical minerals that the world needs

I do not blame mine managers for refusing access. They must comply with labour rules and manage immediate, severe hazards: unstable rock, heat, water, dust, heavy machinery and restricted escape routes.

But protection becomes unfair when every activity labelled ‘underground mining’ is treated as though it involves the same risk exposure. China’s 2012 law improving workplace rights and health rules for women still prohibits underground mine work for female employees. Dozens of countries have similar restrictions. The rule has a protective purpose: women face unique risks in mines (O. S. Mokwena et al. Safety 12, 1; 2026). However, it does not distinguish between repeated shifts and a brief, supervised visit to calibrate a sensor or inspect a monitoring system. Resolving that tension requires regulatory reform.

The timing matters. Modern mining encompasses much more than excavation. Researchers install and test sensors, analyse seismic signals, model ventilation, supervise autonomous equipment, examine cores, operate remote-control systems and plan ecological restoration. Many of these tasks take place entirely on the surface. Others might require limited underground access. The risks are not identical, so the rules should not be either.

I am calling for a task-based system with three pathways.

Demand for lithium is surging: here’s how to make mining more sustainable

Long-duration, high-exposure production work should be subject to the strictest statutory protections. No employer should use inclusion as an excuse to weaken safety requirements, reduce staffing or pressure anyone to accept risks.

Brief visits for research and education, however, should have a lawful pathway. Entry should depend on a site-specific risk assessment, mandatory training, correctly fitted protective equipment, strict time limits, real-time tracking, supervision and an emergency plan. Participation must be voluntary. When these safeguards cannot be guaranteed, or when the same objective can be achieved from the surface, underground entry should not occur.

Candidates for surface-based roles should be assessed on the basis of competence, not underground-access eligibility rules from a different era.
articles.reasoning: The article highlights a significant and positive push towards gender equality and inclusion in the mining research field by advocating for regulatory reform to allow women safer, more equitable access to underground mine research. This change has broad societal impact by challenging outdated labor laws and promoting fair access to scientific and engineering careers, with detailed proposals for modernizing safety regulations.
articles.personality_title: New rules proposed to let women safely work underground in mines
articles.personality_presentation:
**Context** – In many countries, women engineers and researchers are not allowed to enter deep mines. This is because old safety laws treat all underground mining as equally dangerous and often exclude women entirely from going underground.

**What happened** – A female mining professor from China shared her experience of being barred from going underground for research, even though her work involved designing safety systems for mines. She explains that current laws, like China’s 2012 rule, ban women from underground mine work to protect them from risks, but these rules are too strict and do not consider different types of tasks.

**Impact** – The article shows that mining today involves many activities beyond digging, such as testing sensors or controlling equipment remotely, which might be safer and need only short underground visits. By treating all underground work the same, women miss out on important research opportunities. Changing this could allow more women to participate in mining science while still keeping everyone safe.

**What's next step** – The professor suggests creating a new system with three levels of underground access: strict rules for long, risky work; safer, supervised short visits for research; and surface-based jobs judged by skill, not outdated rules. This would require new laws and clear safety plans to make sure women can enter mines safely and fairly.

**One-sentence takeaway** – Updating mining safety rules can open the door for women to do important underground research while staying protected.
articles.personality_title_fr: De nouvelles règles proposées pour permettre aux femmes de travailler en toute sécurité dans les mines souterraines
articles.personality_presentation_fr:
**Contexte** – Dans de nombreux pays, les femmes ingénieures et chercheuses ne sont pas autorisées à entrer dans les mines profondes. Cela est dû à d’anciennes lois de sécurité qui considèrent tous les travaux souterrains comme également dangereux et excluent souvent totalement les femmes.

**Ce qui s’est passé** – Une professeure chinoise en ingénierie minière a raconté son expérience : elle s’est vue refuser l’accès souterrain pour ses recherches, alors même qu’elle concevait des systèmes de sécurité pour les mines. Elle explique que les lois actuelles, comme celle de 2012 en Chine, interdisent aux femmes de travailler sous terre pour les protéger, mais ces règles sont trop strictes et ne prennent pas en compte les différents types de tâches.

**Impact** – L’article montre que le travail minier aujourd’hui va bien au-delà du creusement, avec des activités comme tester des capteurs ou contrôler des machines à distance, qui sont plus sûres et nécessitent parfois seulement de courtes visites souterraines. En traitant tout de la même façon, les femmes sont privées d’opportunités importantes. Changer cela pourrait permettre à plus de femmes de participer à la recherche minière tout en garantissant la sécurité.

**Prochaine étape** – La professeure propose un nouveau système avec trois niveaux d’accès souterrain : des règles strictes pour les travaux longs et dangereux ; des visites courtes et supervisées pour la recherche ; et des postes en surface évalués selon les compétences, pas selon des règles dépassées. Cela demanderait de nouvelles lois et des plans de sécurité clairs pour assurer un accès sûr et équitable.

**Une phrase clé** – Moderniser les règles de sécurité minière peut ouvrir la voie aux femmes pour réaliser des recherches souterraines importantes tout en restant protégées.
articles.personality_title_es: Nuevas reglas propuestas para que las mujeres trabajen de forma segura en minas subterráneas
articles.personality_presentation_es:
**Contexto** – En muchos países, las mujeres ingenieras e investigadoras no pueden entrar en minas profundas. Esto se debe a leyes antiguas de seguridad que tratan todo trabajo subterráneo como igualmente peligroso y suelen excluir a las mujeres.

**Qué pasó** – Una profesora de ingeniería minera en China contó que le prohibieron entrar a la mina para su investigación, aunque diseñaba sistemas de seguridad para minas. Explicó que las leyes actuales, como la de China de 2012, prohíben a las mujeres trabajar bajo tierra para protegerlas, pero estas reglas son demasiado estrictas y no consideran diferentes tipos de tareas.

**Impacto** – El artículo muestra que hoy en día la minería incluye muchas actividades además de excavar, como probar sensores o controlar equipos a distancia, que son más seguras y solo necesitan visitas cortas al subsuelo. Al tratar todo igual, las mujeres pierden oportunidades importantes. Cambiar esto permitiría que más mujeres participen en la investigación minera con seguridad.

**Próximo paso** – La profesora propone un sistema con tres niveles de acceso subterráneo: reglas estrictas para trabajos largos y riesgosos; visitas breves y supervisadas para investigación; y trabajos en superficie evaluados por habilidad, no por reglas antiguas. Esto requeriría nuevas leyes y planes de seguridad claros para garantizar acceso seguro y justo.

**Una frase clave** – Actualizar las reglas de seguridad minera puede permitir que las mujeres realicen investigaciones subterráneas importantes mientras se mantienen protegidas.
articles.image_prompt: A detailed warm-toned painting showing a sturdy mining helmet with a soft glowing light inside, resting beside a delicate compass and a set of scientific instruments like sensors and monitoring devices, all placed at the entrance of a stylized mine shaft that opens into a bright, hopeful landscape, symbolizing the opening of new pathways and careful access for women researchers in underground mining.

articles.title: Reform of all social media should come with Meta changes, UN says
articles.summary: California's attorney general is now looking at TikTok and YouTube to enact teen safety features.
articles.content:
All of social media should be designed to be safe for children, the UN human rights chief has said after Meta settled a massive court case in the US.

Part of the deal the tech giant struck with almost all US states was to add more child safety measures - but Meta also called on TikTok and YouTube to add the same features.

The UN's high commissioner for human rights Volker Türk said governments needed to "step up rather than wait for courts and companies to act".

He added: "Children should not have to wait for a lawsuit to be safe online."

Türk said Meta's proposed changes, which include time limits and parental supervision controls, aligned with what he had been calling for - "but we're not there yet".

In May, Türk's office released a 10-point framework for regulating social media, external.

It included steps such as protecting data privacy and focusing on safer platform design, including better methods of verifying a user's age and not exposing such users to addictive design features.

However, the framework rejected the idea that outright bans on social media use for children was a good idea.
articles.reasoning: The article reports on a significant positive development in social media regulation aimed at protecting children online, with the UN advocating for safer platform designs and governments to take proactive steps. This has broad societal impact by promoting child safety and digital rights, supported by concrete proposals and a framework from the UN.
articles.personality_title: UN urges all social media to improve child safety after Meta agreement
articles.personality_presentation:
**Context** – Social media platforms are widely used by children, but concerns about their safety online have grown. The UN human rights chief has been pushing for better rules to protect young users.

**What happened** – Meta, the company behind Facebook and Instagram, reached a legal agreement in the US to add more safety features for children. These include time limits on use and controls for parents. Following this, the UN called on other platforms like TikTok and YouTube to make similar changes.

**Impact** – This is important because it shows a larger effort to make social media safer for kids everywhere, not just on one platform. The UN also shared a 10-point plan that suggests ways to protect children’s privacy and prevent designs that encourage addictive use. This approach helps children use social media more safely without banning it completely.

**What's next step** – Governments are encouraged to act quickly instead of waiting for lawsuits or company decisions. Platforms like TikTok and YouTube may soon add new safety tools. The UN’s framework could guide future laws and rules to protect children online.

**One-sentence takeaway** – The UN is pushing social media companies and governments to work together to create safer online spaces for children, following Meta’s recent safety commitments.
articles.personality_title_fr: L’ONU appelle tous les réseaux sociaux à renforcer la sécurité des enfants après l’accord avec Meta
articles.personality_presentation_fr:
**Contexte** – Les réseaux sociaux sont très utilisés par les enfants, mais leur sécurité en ligne inquiète de plus en plus. Le chef des droits humains de l’ONU demande de meilleures règles pour protéger les jeunes utilisateurs.

**Ce qui s’est passé** – Meta, la société derrière Facebook et Instagram, a conclu un accord légal aux États-Unis pour ajouter plus de mesures de sécurité pour les enfants, comme des limites de temps et des contrôles parentaux. L’ONU a ensuite demandé à d’autres plateformes comme TikTok et YouTube de faire de même.

**Impact** – Cela montre un effort plus large pour rendre les réseaux sociaux plus sûrs pour les enfants partout, pas seulement sur une seule plateforme. L’ONU a aussi présenté un plan en 10 points pour protéger la vie privée des enfants et éviter les designs qui créent une dépendance. Cette approche aide les enfants à utiliser les réseaux sociaux en toute sécurité sans les interdire.

**Prochaine étape** – Les gouvernements sont encouragés à agir rapidement sans attendre des procès ou des décisions des entreprises. TikTok et YouTube pourraient bientôt ajouter de nouveaux outils de sécurité. Le cadre de l’ONU pourrait guider les futures lois pour protéger les enfants en ligne.

**Résumé en une phrase** – L’ONU pousse les entreprises et les gouvernements des réseaux sociaux à collaborer pour créer des espaces en ligne plus sûrs pour les enfants, suite aux engagements récents de Meta.
articles.personality_title_es: La ONU insta a todas las redes sociales a mejorar la seguridad infantil tras acuerdo con Meta
articles.personality_presentation_es:
**Contexto** – Los niños usan mucho las redes sociales, pero hay preocupaciones sobre su seguridad en línea. El jefe de derechos humanos de la ONU ha pedido mejores reglas para proteger a los jóvenes usuarios.

**Qué pasó** – Meta, la empresa detrás de Facebook e Instagram, llegó a un acuerdo legal en Estados Unidos para añadir más medidas de seguridad para niños, como límites de tiempo y controles parentales. Luego, la ONU pidió a otras plataformas como TikTok y YouTube que hagan cambios similares.

**Impacto** – Esto es importante porque muestra un esfuerzo mayor para hacer que las redes sociales sean más seguras para los niños en todas partes, no solo en una plataforma. La ONU también compartió un plan de 10 puntos que sugiere formas de proteger la privacidad de los niños y evitar diseños que fomentan el uso adictivo. Esta estrategia ayuda a que los niños usen las redes sociales con más seguridad sin prohibirlas.

**Próximo paso** – Se anima a los gobiernos a actuar rápido en lugar de esperar demandas o decisiones de las empresas. TikTok y YouTube podrían pronto añadir nuevas herramientas de seguridad. El marco de la ONU podría guiar futuras leyes para proteger a los niños en línea.

**Resumen en una frase** – La ONU impulsa a empresas y gobiernos a trabajar juntos para crear espacios en línea más seguros para los niños, tras los compromisos recientes de Meta.
articles.image_prompt: A detailed, warm-toned painting of a large, protective hand gently cradling a glowing, stylized smartphone surrounded by softly glowing icons representing social media apps, while a subtle network of interconnected locks and shields weaves around the device symbolizing child safety, parental controls, and responsible platform design.

articles.title: Rock en Seine: Visually impaired spectators enjoy festival with audio description
articles.summary: At Paris's Rock en Seine, visually impaired festival-goers can enjoy concerts through live audio description. The festival is offering dedicated platforms, as well as headphones and receivers provided by the Valentin Haüy Association, a pioneer in audio description in France. Spectators can experience a concert with audio description each day of the music festival, from August 26 to August 30.
articles.content: At Paris's Rock en Seine, visually impaired festival-goers can enjoy concerts through live audio description. The festival is offering dedicated platforms, as well as headphones and receivers provided by the Valentin Haüy Association, a pioneer in audio description in France. Spectators can experience a concert with audio description each day of the music festival, from August 26 to August 30.
articles.source: News and stories on CULTURE, movies, music, literature - France 24
articles.reasoning: The article highlights a meaningful accessibility initiative that enables visually impaired individuals to enjoy a major public cultural event through live audio description, promoting inclusion and equal access to entertainment. The impact is significant for a broad group of people with disabilities and is well detailed.
articles.personality_title: Rock en Seine festival offers live audio description for visually impaired fans
articles.personality_presentation:
**Context** – Rock en Seine is a popular music festival held every year in Paris. Usually, enjoying live concerts can be difficult for people who cannot see well, as they miss out on visual parts of the show.

**What happened** – This year, from August 26 to 30, the festival created special platforms for visually impaired spectators. They provided headphones and receivers so these fans could listen to live audio descriptions. The descriptions explain what is happening on stage during the concerts. The equipment was offered by the Valentin Haüy Association, a group known for helping visually impaired people in France.

**Impact** – This service lets visually impaired people enjoy the festival in a way they couldn’t before. It makes the concerts more accessible and shows how events can include everyone. By hearing detailed descriptions, fans can follow the music and the performers’ actions, making the experience richer and more fun.

**What’s next step** – The success of this project may encourage other festivals and public events to add similar audio descriptions. It could become a common way to make entertainment more inclusive for people with disabilities.

**One-sentence takeaway** – Rock en Seine's live audio description service helps visually impaired fans experience concerts fully and could inspire more accessible events in the future.
articles.personality_title_fr: Le festival Rock en Seine propose une description audio en direct pour les spectateurs malvoyants
articles.personality_presentation_fr:
**Contexte** – Rock en Seine est un festival de musique populaire qui a lieu chaque année à Paris. En général, profiter des concerts en direct peut être difficile pour les personnes malvoyantes, car elles ne voient pas les éléments visuels du spectacle.

**Ce qui s’est passé** – Cette année, du 26 au 30 août, le festival a créé des plateformes spéciales pour les spectateurs malvoyants. Ils ont fourni des casques et des récepteurs pour que ces fans puissent écouter des descriptions audio en direct. Ces descriptions expliquent ce qui se passe sur scène pendant les concerts. Le matériel a été offert par l’Association Valentin Haüy, un groupe reconnu pour son aide aux personnes malvoyantes en France.

**Impact** – Ce service permet aux personnes malvoyantes de profiter du festival d’une manière qu’elles ne pouvaient pas auparavant. Il rend les concerts plus accessibles et montre comment les événements peuvent inclure tout le monde. En entendant des descriptions détaillées, les fans peuvent suivre la musique et les actions des artistes, rendant l’expérience plus riche et plus agréable.

**Prochaine étape** – Le succès de ce projet pourrait encourager d’autres festivals et événements publics à ajouter des descriptions audio similaires. Cela pourrait devenir une manière courante de rendre le divertissement plus inclusif pour les personnes en situation de handicap.

**Résumé en une phrase** – Le service de description audio en direct de Rock en Seine aide les spectateurs malvoyants à vivre pleinement les concerts et pourrait inspirer plus d’événements accessibles à l’avenir.
articles.personality_title_es: El festival Rock en Seine ofrece descripción de audio en vivo para fans con discapacidad visual
articles.personality_presentation_es:
**Contexto** – Rock en Seine es un festival de música popular que se celebra cada año en París. Normalmente, disfrutar de conciertos en vivo puede ser difícil para personas con discapacidad visual porque no pueden ver las partes visuales del espectáculo.

**Qué pasó** – Este año, del 26 al 30 de agosto, el festival creó plataformas especiales para espectadores con discapacidad visual. Proporcionaron auriculares y receptores para que estos fans pudieran escuchar descripciones de audio en vivo. Las descripciones explican lo que sucede en el escenario durante los conciertos. El equipo fue ofrecido por la Asociación Valentin Haüy, un grupo conocido por ayudar a personas con discapacidad visual en Francia.

**Impacto** – Este servicio permite que las personas con discapacidad visual disfruten del festival de una manera que antes no podían. Hace que los conciertos sean más accesibles y muestra cómo los eventos pueden incluir a todos. Al escuchar descripciones detalladas, los fans pueden seguir la música y las acciones de los artistas, haciendo la experiencia más rica y divertida.

**Próximo paso** – El éxito de este proyecto podría animar a otros festivales y eventos públicos a añadir descripciones de audio similares. Podría convertirse en una forma común de hacer el entretenimiento más inclusivo para personas con discapacidad.

**Conclusión en una frase** – El servicio de descripción de audio en vivo de Rock en Seine ayuda a los fans con discapacidad visual a experimentar los conciertos completamente y podría inspirar eventos más accesibles en el futuro.
articles.image_prompt: A warm, detailed painting of a lively outdoor music festival stage with softly glowing headphones resting on a wooden platform, surrounded by gentle silhouettes of sound waves flowing like ribbons toward an abstract figure with closed eyes, symbolizing a visually impaired listener immersed in live audio description.
